input_prompt: Write a 30-second product ad for AeroPress coffee maker. Target: busy professionals who care about coffee quality. Brand voice: confident, modern, no-nonsense.

scenes.narration: You've got a meeting in ten minutes. The office machine is broken. Again.
scenes.visualDescription: Close-up of a generic drip coffee machine with a blinking red error light. Harsh fluorescent office lighting. Shallow depth of field.

scenes.narration: But you don't drink that coffee anyway.
scenes.visualDescription: Hands confidently placing an AeroPress on a clean desk. Morning sunlight streaming in. The AeroPress catches the light. Product hero shot.

scenes.narration: Sixty seconds. Hot water. Press. Done.
scenes.visualDescription: Quick montage: water poured from electric kettle, plunger pressed down with satisfying resistance, rich dark coffee flowing into a ceramic mug. Each action fills 1 second. Warm color grade.

scenes.narration: AeroPress. For people who refuse to drink bad coffee.
scenes.visualDescription: Professional sipping coffee at their desk, slight smile. Pull back to reveal a clean, modern workspace. AeroPress visible in the background. Warm, golden-hour lighting.

input_prompt: Write a 60-second brand film for a sustainable fashion brand called 'Thread'. Their mission is making luxury clothing from recycled ocean plastics. Target audience: environmentally conscious millennials with disposable income.

scenes.visualDescription: Aerial drone shot of a pristine coastline at golden hour. Waves rolling in. No people. The beauty is almost aggressive. Hold for 3 seconds. Then: a single plastic bottle tumbles in the surf.

scenes.narration: Every year, eight million tons of plastic enter the ocean.
scenes.visualDescription: Close-up of weathered plastic debris on wet sand. Macro detail. The texture is almost abstract, almost beautiful. Muted, desaturated color grade.

scenes.narration: We asked: what if that waste became something you actually wanted to wear?
scenes.visualDescription: Match cut: the abstract plastic texture dissolves into the texture of Thread fabric. Close-up of hands running over the material. The fabric has a subtle sheen. Studio lighting, clean background.

scenes.narration: Thread takes ocean-bound plastic and turns it into clothing that lasts. Not fast fashion. Not compromise. Actual luxury.
scenes.visualDescription: Montage: factory hands sorting pellets, weaving machines in motion, a tailor fitting a jacket on a model. Each shot is composed like a portrait. Warm lighting, earth tones.

scenes.narration: Because the most sustainable thing you can own is something you never throw away.
scenes.visualDescription: Model wearing Thread jacket walks along the same coastline from scene 0. Camera at eye level. They're not posing, they're just walking. The beach is clean now. Golden hour.

input_prompt: Write a 90-second tutorial on 'How to set up Google Analytics 4 for your Shopify store'. Target: small business owners who aren't technical. Keep it simple, no jargon.

expected_output.title: Google Analytics on Shopify in 3 Minutes

scenes.narration: If you're running a Shopify store and you don't know where your customers are coming from, you're flying blind. Let's fix that in under three minutes.
scenes.visualDescription: Screen recording: Shopify dashboard with analytics tab open showing zeros. Cursor circles the empty graphs. Clean, bright screen capture.

scenes.narration: Step one. Go to analytics.google.com and click 'Start measuring'. Use the same Google account you use for everything else. Name your account after your store.
scenes.visualDescription: Screen recording: browser navigating to analytics.google.com. Click 'Start measuring'. Type store name into account field. Each click highlighted with a cursor spotlight effect.

scenes.narration: Step two. When it asks for a property, that's just Google's word for 'your website'. Put in your store URL. Pick your timezone and currency.
scenes.visualDescription: Screen recording: property setup page. Cursor fills in the URL field, selects timezone dropdown, picks currency. Jargon like 'property' gets a callout bubble: 'Property = Your Website'.

scenes.narration: Step three. Grab the measurement ID. It starts with G-something. Copy it. Now go to your Shopify admin, click Online Store, then Preferences. Paste it in the Google Analytics box. Hit save.
scenes.visualDescription: Split screen: left side shows GA4 with measurement ID highlighted. Right side shows Shopify admin > Online Store > Preferences. Arrow connects them visually. Paste animation.

scenes.narration: That's it. Give it 24 hours and you'll start seeing real data: where your visitors come from, what they look at, and what makes them buy. No more guessing.
scenes.visualDescription: Screen recording: GA4 realtime dashboard showing actual visitor data flowing in. Numbers ticking up. Map showing visitor locations. The data is alive.

input_prompt: Write a 45-second talking head video: 'Why most startups fail at marketing'. Speaker is a marketing agency CEO. Platform: LinkedIn. Tone: authoritative but not arrogant.

expected_output.title: The Marketing Mistake That Kills Startups

scenes.narration: I've worked with over 200 startups. Want to know the number one reason their marketing fails? They build the product first and ask 'how do we sell this?' second.
scenes.visualDescription: Speaker directly to camera. Clean background, slightly off-center framing. Confident posture. One small gesture on 'number one reason'. Warm but not soft lighting.

scenes.narration: That's backwards. The companies that win? They start with the customer's language. The exact words people use when they're frustrated. When they're searching. When they're complaining to their friends.
scenes.visualDescription: Same speaker, slightly wider frame now. Uses hands to emphasize 'exact words'. Energy builds. Cut to B-roll: someone typing a frustrated search query on their phone.
scenes.onScreenText: Start with their words. Not yours.

scenes.narration: If you can't describe what you do in the words your customer already uses, you don't have a marketing problem. You have a listening problem.
scenes.visualDescription: Back to speaker. Closer frame. Direct eye contact. Slight pause after 'listening problem'. The pause lands. No movement, just conviction.

scenes.narration: Talk to ten customers this week. Write down exactly how they describe the problem. That's your marketing. That's it.
scenes.visualDescription: Speaker, medium frame. Opens hands in a 'that simple' gesture. Slight smile. Holds the look for 1 second after finishing. Cut to branded end card.

input_prompt: Write a 15-second Instagram Reel for a protein bar called 'FuelUp'. Target: gym-goers aged 20-30. Vibe: energetic, punchy, not corporate. Brand voice: like a gym buddy, not a nutritionist.

scenes.visualDescription: POV: someone just finished a hard workout. Heavy breathing sound. Phone screen shows 11:47 PM. Gym is empty. Dark, gritty, handheld camera shake.
Hand reaches into gym bag. Pulls out a FuelUp bar. Rips the wrapper. The tear sound is satisfying and loud. Close-up of the bar texture. Handheld, raw lighting.
Person takes a bite. Nods. Walks out of gym into the night. Door swings shut behind them. Confident walk. Street lights. Low angle.
FuelUp logo animates in. Clean. Simple. The wrapper from scene 1 sits crumpled in frame. Real, not styled.
